latest_release.name: v1.34.0
latest_release.body:
1.34.0 adds two migrations, and both only add. 0106 adds a nullable
`bookmarks` column to maps; 0107 adds a nullable `manifest_key` to maps and to
map layers, each with a partial unique index. Instances still on 1.33.0 keep
serving while they run. `EXTENSION_API_VERSION` moves from 23 to 26. Publish
manifest version 2 is a preview: nothing sends it yet, it may change in any
release, and its `maps` section is only checked in a dry run. Version 1 is
unchanged.

### Added
- A dataset made by an analysis shows a "Derived from" row in its Details list, linking the source dataset, naming the operation and linking a second input when there is one.
- Maps hold bookmarks: a name and an area, with an optional rotation and tilt, in display order. The maps API and the SDKs carry an optional `bookmarks` list (up to 100) on create and update, and the map and shared map responses always return one. The ArcGIS web map import carries a web map's bookmarks. The map builder has a Bookmarks panel to add the current view, rename, reorder and delete bookmarks, and the viewer, share links and embeds have a Bookmarks control that jumps to one.
- The publish manifest accepts `manifest_version: "2"`, which requires a `client` object naming the publishing app, and an `upload:<job_id>` source that names a file the caller uploaded with `POST /ingest/upload`. An upload source needs a `checksum`, the SHA-256 of the uploaded file, and apply refuses the entry when the file doesn't match it. The upload's own job becomes the import, and uploading the same file again for an unchanged entry answers `skip`. Version 2 is a preview and may change in any release until the desktop connectors ship; version 1 is stable.
- Manifest version 2 datasets take `visibility`, `collection` and `attributes`, and the request takes `public_fallback`. Visibility comes from the explicit field, never from the publication intent, which sets only the record status: a create without it is private, and an update without it keeps the current level. A refused `public` is error `A020` for that entry, or `internal` with warning `A020` when `public_fallback` is `"internal"`; a publish key's update that would publish a public dataset counts as a refused `public`. The restriction on public visibility applies only to an entry that names `public`. A `collection` by id or name is resolved before anything is queued, and a refusal is warning `A033`. `attributes` save per-column title, description and units by the column name in the uploaded file, and a name that matches no column is job warning `A092`. Each result gains `messages`, and a dry run warns `A053` when the dataset's features were edited since the last publish. Job status `warnings` gain the kinds `manifest_collection_refused`, `manifest_attribute_unmatched` and `manifest_public_fallback`, the last when public is refused as a job runs or is accepted and the entry's fallback shares it with the organization instead.
- Manifest version 2 takes `maps`, each with its layers, and a dry run checks them: a map key on a map the caller can't edit is `A050`, a layer whose dataset doesn't exist, hasn't finished publishing or can't be read is `A052`, unless the same request's `datasets` publishes that key, unknown `style_config` and `label_config` keys are dropped with `A062`, and a column the dataset lacks is `A063`. In version 2 `datasets` may be empty when `maps` isn't, and the response gains `maps`, one result per map with its `messages`. Maps aren't written yet: a request with maps that isn't a dry run is refused with 422 before anything is applied. Map and map layer keys are unique across the server and within their map; a duplicate starts without them and a transfer keeps them.

### Changed
- The PostGIS table name under a dataset's title shows only to signed-in users who can edit the dataset. The Details list still shows it to everyone.
- A dashboard panel says once at the top that its numbers follow the map view, instead of on every card. Wher

detail.readme:
GeoLens

An open-source, self-hosted alternative to ArcGIS Online: a spatial data catalog with maps, stories and dashboards.

Live demo · Quick start · Documentation · Connect QGIS or code · Discussions

[English](README.md) · [Español](README.es.md) · [Français](README.fr.md) · [Deutsch](README.de.md) · [简体中文](README.zh.md) [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/geolens-io/geolens?style=flat-square&label=release)](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/releases/latest) [![CI status](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/geolens-io/geolens/ci.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=CI)](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-2563eb?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.securityscorecards.dev/projects/github.com/geolens-io/geolens/badge)](https://securityscorecards.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/geolens-io/geolens) [![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15857/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15857)


Manhattan's buildings at their surveyed roof heights, colored by construction era, with the subway network. Browse the demo's maps.

GeoLens is for teams whose spatial data is spread across file shares, databases, web services and STAC catalogs. It puts that data in one searchable catalog and records where each dataset came from. Teams build maps, stories and dashboards in the browser and share them with groups or the public, and QGIS, scripts and AI agents read the same data through OGC API and STAC. It runs on your own servers with Docker Compose, sends no telemetry and is licensed under Apache 2.0. The [demo](https://demo.getgeolens.com) needs no install or account; sign in with Google, GitHub or Microsoft to use the map builder. Demo data may be wiped at any time. ## Quick start You need Git, curl and Docker with the Compose plugin, with 8 GB of memory available to Docker. ```sh curl -fsSL https://getgeolens.com/install.sh | sh # clone, generate secrets, start the stack cd geolens grep '^GEOLENS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=' .env # the generated admin password ``` Open http://localhost:8080 and sign in as `admin` with that password. [Install](#install) covers verifying the script, building from source and running in production. ## A closer look

Search by meaning: "where storms hit the coast" finds hurricane tracks and coastal exposure layers.
An ArcGIS Online web map imported into GeoLens. Its colors, popups, outlines and zoom ranges carried over.

A story walks readers through a map chapter by chapter.
A dashboard puts indicators, charts and lists beside the map, and they follow what's in view.
## How it fits together ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph IN ["Bring data in"] F["Files
GeoPackage · Shapefile · GeoParquet
GeoTIFF · COPC · 3D Tiles"] DB["Databases
PostGIS tables · SQL Server"] SVC["Services
ArcGIS · WFS · OGC API Features"] ST["Remote STAC assets"] end subgraph GL ["GeoLens"] CAT["Catalog
search · metadata · provenance"] MB["Map builder
styles · 3D · analysis · stories · dashboards · sharing"] STD["Open APIs
OGC API · STAC · DCAT · tiles"] end subgraph OUT ["Use it anywhere"] WEB["Browsers and embeds"] GIS["QGIS · ArcGIS · CesiumJS"] CODE["curl · Python · TypeScript · DuckDB"] AG["AI agents via MCP"] end F & DB & SVC & ST --> CAT CAT --> MB --> WEB CAT --> STD --> GIS & CODE & AG ``` ## One catalog for scattered data - Upload Shapefile, GeoPackage, GeoJSON, GeoParquet, FlatGeobuf, KML/KMZ, zipped File Geodatabase, CSV, Excel or GeoTIFF (converted to Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF). 3D Tiles and COPC point clouds are hosted for CesiumJS, QGIS and Potree. - Serve tables already in GeoLens's PostGIS database in place, import WFS, ArcGIS and OGC API Features layers and SQL Server tables and refresh them on demand, or reference remote STAC assets without copying them. - Draw new datasets in the browser. - Find data with fuzzy search, or by meaning once an embedding provider is configured. Filter by type, place and time, group datasets into collections, edit metadata and restore a dataset's previous version after a replacement. ### Coming from ArcGIS Online `geolens arcgis inventory` reads an ArcGIS Online organization or a self-hosted ArcGIS portal and reports what would carry over to GeoLens. It changes nothing and needs no GeoLens instance. `geolens arcgis migrate` then moves layers, files and web maps into GeoLens with their owners, folders and sharing, and writes a loss report of what didn't carry over. The [CLI guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/cli/#arcgis-migration) walks through it. ## Know where every dataset came from


A dataset imported from the USGS earthquake service.

Each dataset records where it came from: an uploaded file, a database table, a service, a STAC item or a drawing in the browser. Imported datasets also record when they were last refreshed, and with an update cadence GeoLens marks them fresh, due or overdue. For services and STAC sources, GeoLens also checks that the source still answers, and for services it flags upstream schema changes before they reach your maps. If a service disappears, the imported copy keeps working. ## Build and share maps - Point, symbol, heatmap, cluster, line, arrow, fill, 3D extrusion, raster and hillshade layers, with data-driven styles, labels, icons, patterns, filters and popups. Terrain comes from your own elevation models. - Buffer, centroid, clip, dissolve, spatial join, select by location, measure and intersect. Most operations preview on the map, and each result is saved as a new dataset, from the builder or the CLI. - Story maps walk readers through a map scene by scene, with Markdown text, images, buttons and separators. Dashboards put indicators, charts, filters and Markdown notes beside a map. A Map data panel shows the rows behind each layer, as a table or a list. - Share a dataset, map or story with groups, with everyone signed in, or with the public. Public maps and published stories show their title and image when pasted into Slack, Teams or social posts, and maps embed in other sites with private tokens. - The interface is in English, Spanish, French, German and Simplified Chinese. ## Use the data from anywhere Vector datasets are OGC API Features collections, the catalog is OGC API Records and STAC, and every layer has a tile URL. You can try this against the demo without an account (the second command needs `jq`): ```sh # Search the catalog (OGC API Records) curl "https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/collections/datasets/items?q=volcanic%20eruptions" # Read the top match with a CQL2 filter (OGC API Features): eruptions of VEI 6 or larger ID=$(curl -s "https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/collections/datasets/items?q=volcanic%20eruptions&limit=1" | jq -r '.features[0].id') curl -G "https://demo.getgeolens.com/api/collections/$ID/items" \ --data-urlencode "filter=vei >= 6" -d limit=3 ``` QGIS adds the same API as an OGC API Features connection, as the [QGIS guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/api/qgis/) shows. The [GeoLens plugin for QGIS](https://github.com/geolens-io/qgis-geolens-plugin) adds catalog search, private datasets and edits that sync back to GeoLens.


QGIS reading the demo over OGC API Features, without a plugin.

| Standard | Where | Use it with | |---|---|---| | OGC API Features, with CQL2 filtering and queryables | `/api/collections/{id}/items` | QGIS, ArcGIS, GDAL/OGR and other OGC API clients | | OGC API Records | `/api/collections/datasets/items` | Catalog search from other portals and tools | | STAC API 1.0 | `/api/stac/` | STAC clients such as pystac-client and STAC Browser | | DCAT 3, DCAT-US 3.0 and GeoDCAT-AP as JSON-LD | `/api/datasets/dcat/`, `/api/datasets/dcat-us/3.0/`, `/api/datasets/geodcat-ap/` | Harvesting into national and EU open-data portals | | Vector tiles and COG raster tiles | a tile URL on every layer | MapLibre, OpenLayers, Leaflet | | 3D Tiles and COPC | each 3D dataset's page | CesiumJS, QGIS, Potree | Data exports as GeoJSON, Shapefile, GeoPackage, CSV, FlatGeobuf, GeoParquet, PMTiles or Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF. The `geolens` CLI publishes files and applies catalog manifests, Python and TypeScript SDKs cover the API, and an MCP server lets AI agents search the catalog and, with a `map_author` API key, create and style maps. The [API reference](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/api/) and [SDK guides](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/sdk/) document them, and the [examples gallery](https://geolens-io.github.io/geolens-examples/) has runnable code for MapLibre, Leaflet, OpenLayers, the ArcGIS Maps SDK, QGIS and DuckDB. ## Optional AI GeoLens can answer questions about a dataset, edit maps from plain-language requests, draft metadata and search in natural language. It works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, including a local server such as Ollama, and with Claude through Anthropic, Microsoft Foundry, Amazon Bedrock or Google Vertex AI. AI stays off until an administrator configures a provider, and every workflow works without it. ## Install [Quick start](#quick-start) has the install command. The [Install Guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/quickstart/install/) lists the versions, memory and ports it expects. Each [release](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/releases) includes a `SHA256SUMS` file for checking `install.sh` before you run it. To build from source instead, clone the repository and run `bash scripts/install.sh`; the first build takes 5-10 minutes. Newer releases also include `install.sh.intoto.jsonl`, a signed build provenance record, unless signing it failed for that release. The checksum file can only show that a download wasn't corrupted, because it ships in the same release. The provenance shows that `install.sh` came from the release tag in this repository. To check it, download both files from the release and run the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/): ```bash gh attestation verify install.sh --repo geolens-io/geolens \ --bundle install.sh.intoto.jsonl --source-ref refs/tags/vX.Y.Z \ --signer-workflow geolens-io/geolens/.github/workflows/publish.yml ``` For production, read the [cloud deployment guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/quickstart/cloud-deployment/), which also lists what an external database needs. Docker Compose is the supported path, and [geolens-deployments](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens-deployments) has a community-maintained Helm chart and Terraform recipes for AWS ECS Fargate and Azure Container Apps. The bundled database is backed up daily, and the [backup guide](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/admin/backups/) covers off-site copies and restores. [UPGRADING.md](UPGRADING.md) covers upgrades and rollback, [RUNBOOK.md](RUNBOOK.md) covers operations, and the [Configuration Reference](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/quickstart/configuration/) lists every setting. ## Your first dataset With the [CLI](https://docs.getgeolens.com/guides/cli/) installed, publish the sample file from the install directory: ```sh geolens login http://localhost:8080/api # your admin username and password geolens publish examples/manifests/first-catalog/city-parks.geojson --name "City Parks" ``` `geolens publish` prints the new dataset's URL. To manage a whole catalog, describe the sources in a `geolens.yaml` manifest and run `geolens apply`; [`examples/manifests/`](examples/manifests/) has templates. To load the demo's maps and datasets, export `GEOLENS_ADMIN_PASSWORD` from `.env` and run `python scripts/seed-showcase.py --username admin`. The script needs Python 3.10+ and `httpx` and downloads public data from about a dozen sources; [scripts/README.md](scripts/README.md) has the sizes and options. ## Privacy and access - GeoLens sends no telemetry. Apart from the default basemap tiles and the remote services or STAC sources your users register, it makes outbound calls only for features an administrator turns on. [EGRESS.md](EGRESS.md) lists them and explains how to run air-gapped. - Your data stays readable without GeoLens. Vector datasets are ordinary PostGIS tables in a `data` schema, rasters are Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs in your own storage (local disk, S3/MinIO or Azure Blob), and the catalog exports through OGC API, STAC and DCAT. - Sign-in uses local accounts or OAuth 2.0/OIDC (Google, Microsoft, GitHub or a generic provider), with roles, groups, per-dataset permissions, per-user API keys and an audit log. Self-registration is off by default. - Features released in this repository stay free. [EDITIONS.md](EDITIONS.md) describes the optional paid support and add-ons. ## Known limitations - The supported install, Docker Compose, runs on one host. For high availability, run several replicas of the API, worker, frontend and Titiler against a managed PostgreSQL with automatic failover, shared object storage and one Valkey or Redis cache. With Azure Blob or local storage, API and worker replicas also need a shared staging volume, since only S3 keeps uploads in the bucket. Local storage keeps every file on that volume, so Titiler replicas mount it too. [geolens-deployments](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens-deployments) has a community-maintained Helm chart, Terraform recipes for AWS and Azure, and guides for AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and DigitalOcean. GeoLens itself doesn't cluster the database or read from replicas. - One organization per deployment. - Terrain rendering assumes elevation in meters; other vertical units render exaggerated. - GeoLens's own REST API can change between minor releases (the standards endpoints follow their specifications). The [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) lists contract changes. When a change breaks callers, the old form keeps working for the later of the next minor release and 90 days, and the CHANGELOG records its removal date. That covers REST routes and fields, the map and dashboard JSON clients write, and CLI commands and flags; the SDKs follow the API, and MCP tool names and arguments aren't covered. ## Contributing Bug reports, fixes, translations and docs are welcome. [CONTRIBUTING](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers setup and tests, and [ARCHITECTURE](.github/ARCHITECTURE.md) maps the code. The [QGIS plugin](https://github.com/geolens-io/qgis-geolens-plugin), [examples](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens-examples) and [deployments](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens-deployments) repositories take issues and pull requests too. Ask questions in [GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/discussions), report bugs in [Issues](https://github.com/geolens-io/geolens/issues), and report security problems privately as described in [SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md). The [roadmap](https://docs.getgeolens.com/roadmap/) shows what's planned. ## Built on GeoLens is built on these open source projects. Thanks to everyone who maintains them. - [PostgreSQL](https://www.postgresql.org/) and [PostGIS](https://postgis.net/) hold the catalog and every vector dataset, and [pgvector](https://github.com/pgvector/pgvector) stores the embeddings behind search by meaning. - [GDAL](https://gdal.org/) reads the files and services GeoLens imports and writes the formats it exports, and [PROJ](https://proj.org/) handles coordinate transformations. - [TiTiler](https://developmentseed.org/titiler/) serves raster tiles from Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs. - [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) serves the API, and [Procrastinate](https://procrastinate.readthedocs.io/) runs background jobs with PostgreSQL as the queue. - [MapLibre GL JS](https://maplibre.org/) draws the maps, [deck.gl](https://deck.gl/) and [loaders.gl](https://loaders.gl/) render 3D Tiles and point clouds, and [Terra Draw](https://terradraw.io/) handles drawing and editing. - The web app is written in [React](https://react.dev/). These names belong to their owners, and listing them doesn't mean they endorse GeoLens; see [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md#other-projects-names). ## License GeoLens is licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). The GeoLens name, logo and brand assets are not covered by this license; see [TRADEMARKS.md](TRADEMARKS.md). Sample-data attribution is in [THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md](THIRD_PARTY_DATA.md). The web app serves the license notices for the code it bundles at `/third-party-licenses.txt`, and the backend image's copyleft notices are in [backend/licenses](backend/licenses/). Project policies: [editions](EDITIONS.md) · [support](SUPPORT.md) · [governance](GOVERNANCE.md) · [maintainers](MAINTAINERS.md) · [security](.github/SECURITY.md) · [release process](RELEASE.md) · [egress & air-gap](EGRESS.md)
